producer_report.summary: Root cause: the lists that declare the binary's build inputs (the BUILD_PATHS constant and the ci.yml athena-bin cache key) were checked for shape but never against the files the build really includes. Fix: a new test, crates/athena-core/tests/build_inputs.rs, derives the compiled-in set and fails, naming each missing path, unless BUILD_PATHS and every athena-bin hashFiles line of the real ci.yml cover it. The set is every production include_str!/include_bytes! target under crates/ and xtask/, plus the manifests, rust-toolchain.toml and setup.sh. A glob form the matcher can't read fails and is named. status.rs gets `list_touches(list, paths)`, which `touches_build` now calls, so production and the check share one matcher and a test can hand in the old five-entry list. BUILD_PATHS grows to eight entries (adds athena.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, docs/system-facts.md); defaults.toml is left out because no production code compiles it in. The stale-build message and a drain.rs doc comment were updated to match. CHANGELOG.md and a new D154 name the cause and how the three prior jobs are handled. The ci.yml change is a header comment only. Negative fixtures: the pre-fix kq9v key, a key without system-facts, an unreadable glob, a new file outside crates/, and the old five-entry list. I ran fmt, clippy, policy, drain, refusal_corpus and the status unit tests; the full workspace test run is left to Athena.

criteria_check.criterion: The change description (CHANGELOG.md entry) names the root cause: declared input lists were checked for structure but not against the real compiled-in inputs, citing jobs 20261031-172040-kq9v, 20261017-173508-0wtc and 20261025-214509-y179 and saying how each prior result is addressed or why it is out of scope.
criteria_check.evidence: Read the new Unreleased entry in CHANGELOG.md. It states the cause in those words, and says kq9v's fix and policy check are kept with the BUILD_PATHS check added, 0wtc is met at the class level only with the ontology untouched, and y179 keeps its code with the measure-first stage out of scope. `cargo test -p athena-core --test build_inputs` passes unreleased_changelog_names_the_cause_and_jobs, which asserts the three ids and `compiled-in` in the Unreleased section.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test under crates/athena-core derives the input set from every include_str!/include_bytes! target under crates/*/src plus BUILD_PATHS, and asserts each is covered by the athena-bin hashFiles globs in .github/workflows/ci.yml (all jobs) and by BUILD_PATHS; it reads ci.yml rather than a copy.
criteria_check.evidence: crates/athena-core/tests/build_inputs.rs: production_includes() scans the include literals, compiled_in_files() adds the manifests, and declared_inputs_cover_the_real_compiled_in_inputs calls check_build_paths(&BUILD_PATHS, ..) and check_keys(&ci_yml(), ..). ci_yml() reads .github/workflows/ci.yml from disk, check_keys covers every `key: athena-bin-` line, and every_athena_bin_key_line_is_read asserts there are nine. The test passes. Scope note: the required set is the include targets plus the manifests, rust-toolchain.toml and setup.sh, and it excludes BUILD_PATHS entries that no include names (crates/, xtask/, Cargo.lock beyond the fixed list) because those are directory or fixed roots, not include targets.

open_issues: Departure from the plan, small: I also edited the doc comment in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (line 109) to list the three added paths, since it enumerates the build paths. The plan said to do so only if it listed paths; it does.

The new test and xtask/tests/policy.rs scan the includes with separate copies of the same logic, as planned. They share a known-target floor and are named as a pair in the test, D154 and the ci.yml header. xtask is out of scope, so policy.rs does not name the new test.
The hardcoded count of nine athena-bin key lines in every_athena_bin_key_line_is_read mirrors policy.rs (six restore, three save); adding a CI job changes it in both places.
I extended BUILD_PATHS before first running the test, so I did not observe the real BUILD_PATHS failing; fixture E shows the old five-entry list failing with the named paths.
Two of the CHANGELOG/D154 claims about prior jobs come from the brief's summaries, not their records, which are absent from the snapshot.
mistakes: Initial test file was not rustfmt-clean (two spots); fixed with cargo fmt --all and re-checked.
I changed BUILD_PATHS before running the test against it, so I did not see the real list fail first.
learnings: regex is a normal dependency of athena-core, so integration tests under crates/athena-core/tests can use it with no new dependency.
xtask/tests/policy.rs already had a ci.yml key check against an independent include scan, so the new test overlaps it by design; BUILD_PATHS had no such check.

BUILD_PATHS has three consumers: touches_build (drain rebuild), stale_build_line (git pathspec) and the drain.rs docs. Tests assert 'stale build' only as a line prefix, so extending the list broke none.
The brief's word rules apply to untracked files too; the policy test reads only tracked files, so I reread the new file against the word list by hand.
desires: Permission to run the whole `cargo test --workspace` once more cheaply, or a per-target timing, to avoid guessing which targets are affected.
